decisions.executionNote: Key is in the left workspace and lock on the right. Begin elbow-up left approach with open gripper; adapt grasp location from live views.
Continue left elbow-up approach, rotating fingers toward the tabletop while retaining clearance.
Advance toward the left-side key while completing the downward-facing grasp orientation.
Align left fingers downward and move over the key base; remaining offset will be checked in the wrist view before closure.
Translate the downward-facing left gripper toward the key shaft near its bow, using the wrist-image offset; remain open.
Key has shifted slightly. Refine wrist alignment over the lower shaft and match its in-plane angle before closing.
Center the lower shaft between the left jaws and finish matching the key angle with small lateral corrections.
Correct the final lateral shaft offset, then close the left gripper for pickup; retention remains to be checked by lifting.
Corrected tensor after zero-motion rejection. Finish closing and begin a small vertical retention-check lift.
Key is visible between the closed left jaws. Lift vertically beyond 5 cm while keeping the grasp closed.
Carry the retained key upward toward a central handover and rotate its bow toward the right. Start the right receiving arm in its elbow-up approach.
Raise and position the left-held key for transfer while the right arm rotates inward, keeping the arms separated.
Orient the key bow toward the right receiver. Continue the right elbow-up inward approach while the left grasp stays fixed in position.
Bring the right fingers toward a horizontal bow grasp, keeping the left-held key steady and maintaining elbow-up continuity.
Finish the right horizontal receiving orientation and approach the bow with a partly open gripper; left remains closed.
Advance the right fingers onto the exposed key bow and lower slightly to match its height. Keep the donor grip closed.
Seat the right jaws slightly farther onto the exposed bow and close for handover while the left hand still supports the key.
The bow tilted during receiver closure, so reopen the right jaws and adjust slightly lower and deeper before transferring support.
Give the tilted bow clearance and lower the open receiving jaws incrementally; check image response before another grasp.
Center the exposed bow in the right wrist view with a small downward and lateral correction, keeping both hands separated at the grasp surfaces.
Continue the measured bow-centering correction in the right wrist image before closing the receiver.
The key has slipped onto the table. Withdraw the right receiver and reopen/reorient the left gripper for a fresh pickup rather than assuming transfer.
Lower the open left hand toward the fallen key while aligning across its shaft. Keep the right hand clear in its own workspace.
Approach the key's middle shaft for a fresh pickup, with the receiving hand stationary and clear.
Raise slightly for clearance while aligning the left jaws parallel to the fallen key shaft; avoid further tabletop pushing.
Increase clearance above the table and align over the middle of the shaft for a controlled second grasp.
Use the head view to place the left grasp over the key shaft, descending with the shaft aligned between the open jaws.
Make a small wrist-guided correction toward the shaft center and approach grasp height slowly.
Center the middle shaft with a short lateral motion and begin closing the left jaws without further descent.
Finish closing on the key shaft, pause for settling, then make a small vertical retention check.
Lift the key with the left jaws closed and verify it remains attached before retrying the handover.
The key did not remain fixed in the wrist view during lifting. Reopen and move farther along the shaft so it lies inside, rather than ahead of, the finger contact region.
Withdraw the right receiver for clearance. Bring the open left contact region farther over the key shaft and descend slowly.
The shaft is now inside the finger contact region. Make the final small centering and height correction, then begin closing.
Correct the remaining sideways bow offset before completing closure; do not descend further into the table.
Close fully around the centered bow and lift gently to test retention, keeping the right arm clear.
Continue the vertical retention check with closed jaws, comparing key motion in both views before attempting another handover.
The key remains on the table. Reopen and place the left jaws over the shaft rather than the bow, then approach a lower grasp height.
Place the finger contact region on the centered lower shaft and lower gently for a deeper grasp before closing.
Close fully at the centered shaft without further downward pressure, then test retention with a short lift.
Lift slowly with the left jaws closed and check whether the key follows rigidly rather than remaining on the table.
The key follows the left hand rigidly. Raise it and orient the exposed bow toward the right receiver while keeping the donor on the left.
Raise the retained key to transfer height and align the open right receiver with the exposed bow, stopping short of contact.
Align the right finger contact region with the exposed bow, accounting for the wrist-to-fingertip offset. Keep the donor fixed.
Advance the right jaws onto the bow with a small lateral correction from the side view, retaining left support.
Correct receiver lateral alignment using the donor view and finger-axis offset; the bow is still securely supported by the left hand.
Close the aligned right jaws around the exposed bow while holding the left grasp steady; verify before releasing the donor.
The receiver appears just short of the bow. Reopen slightly, seat the fingers a few millimeters deeper, then close with donor support.
The right jaws overlap the bow. Gradually release the left donor and withdraw upward slightly, keeping the receiver fully closed to verify transfer.
The key fell when the donor opened, so transfer was not retained. Clear the right receiver and keep the left open for another controlled pickup.
Reapproach the visible aligned shaft with the left gripper open while retracting the right hand. Stop above grasp height for visual correction.
Use a small above-table translation to refine the shaft-to-finger contact offset before descending; right receiver stays clear.
Use the measured image response to place the lower shaft inside the left contact region while descending to the previously effective grasp height.
Shift the left contact region back from the bow onto the lower shaft, then start closure at the known pickup height.
Complete closure without further lateral contact, then lift slightly to judge whether the key is retained.
Lift with the left jaws closed and compare key motion against the table to test this grasp before proceeding.
The key stayed on the table. Reopen and move the contact region along the shaft rather than beyond the bow, with a measured return to pickup height.
The lower shaft now lies centered in the contact region. Close with only a millimetric height correction and hold still to settle.
Lift the closed left grasp vertically and verify rigid retention before a deeper, carefully supported handover.
Raise the retained key and bring its bow closer to the midline, while approaching with the open right receiver from its own side.
